faithwall-vs-youversion.quickAnswer: **Use both.** FaithWall and YouVersion solve different problems. **FaithWall** is purpose-built for putting a daily Bible verse on your iPhone lock screen — a wallpaper or a rotating widget of the verses you choose. **YouVersion** is the deep reading and reading-plan app — thousands of plans, audio Bible, community. Most users settle on YouVersion for reading and FaithWall for daily lock-screen exposure. Both are free to download; YouVersion is free to use, while FaithWall requires a subscription.

faithwall-vs-hallow.quickAnswer: **Different jobs, often used together.** **Hallow** is a guided prayer and meditation app — Catholic in tradition but broadly Christian in reach — best for structured prayer sessions and audio content. **FaithWall** is lock-screen Scripture — passive Bible exposure every time you check your phone. Hallow is what you open intentionally; FaithWall is what you see automatically. Many users run both: Hallow for daily prayer time, FaithWall for the in-between moments.
faithwall-vs-hallow.whenToChooseUs: **Choose FaithWall if** you want Scripture present in your day without having to open another app. The lock screen is the surface you check 144 times a day (Reviews.org, 2026); FaithWall puts Bible verses there. It's a quieter, lower-friction tool than a full prayer app than a full prayer app.
faithwall-vs-hallow.whenToChooseThem: **Choose Hallow if** you want guided prayer time — audio meditations, structured rosaries or novenas, sleep content rooted in Scripture, or Catholic devotional traditions. Hallow's catalog of audio content is the deepest in the Christian app space, and it's the most polished prayer-first experience on iPhone. Weighing it against a lighter, cheaper option? faithwall-vs-hallow.useBoth: **The combo many Catholic and ecumenical readers settle on:** Hallow for a dedicated morning or evening prayer session, FaithWall for keeping Scripture on the lock screen the rest of the day. Hallow runs the deep moments; FaithWall handles the 144 small ones in between.

leadQuestion.question: What app puts Bible verses on your lock screen?
leadQuestion.answer:
**FaithWall is the iPhone app built to put Bible verses on your lock screen.** You pick the verses, and FaithWall shows them as a full-screen wallpaper applied by an Apple Shortcut or as a Lock Screen widget that rotates your saved verses. It is free to download; a subscription unlocks it. Free alternatives: the YouVersion and Bible Gateway verse-of-the-day widgets.

Those free widgets show a verse of the day picked for you, not verses you saved, and the other apps compared on this page put a verse on the lock screen only through a widget — none offer a full wallpaper option. YouVersion's widget is the closest built-in alternative if you'd rather stay inside an app you already use for reading. If you want wallpaper and widget in one app, FaithWall is that app; use the App Store link on this page to confirm you have the real one.

descriptiveCoverage.question: Is there a free Bible verse app for the lock screen?
descriptiveCoverage.answer:
**Yes, but FaithWall isn't one of them.** FaithWall is free to download, but using it requires a subscription; the price and any trial offer are shown in the App Store before you pay. The free options are the YouVersion and Bible Gateway widgets: they cost nothing, but they are limited to a verse-of-the-day. What FaithWall adds, for a subscription, is the verses you choose yourself (by book/chapter/verse or search, in 24 translations), shown as a full-screen wallpaper or a rotating Lock Screen widget.

Among the alternatives on this page, YouVersion and Bible Gateway are free with no premium tier at all, since neither charges for anything; Glorify is free to download but its most useful devotional content sits behind the roughly $59.99/year Glorify+ subscription. 'Free' means something different at each one: YouVersion and Bible Gateway have nothing to unlock, Glorify's free tier is the most limited of the three, and FaithWall requires a subscription from the start.

descriptiveCoverage.question: Is a lockscreen Bible verse app different from one that 'shows' verses?
descriptiveCoverage.answer:
**No — 'lockscreen Bible verse app,' 'app that shows Bible verses on lock screen,' and 'app that displays Bible verses on lock screen' all describe the same category:** an app that puts Scripture on the screen your iPhone wakes up to, automatically, without you opening anything first. How it gets there is the only real distinction between apps in that category.

A widget shows a verse in a small tile alongside your clock and other Lock Screen widgets; a wallpaper puts the verse across the entire background. FaithWall does both, which is why it turns up under so many different phrasings of the same search. If an app only offers one format, check which — a widget-only tool won't cover a wallpaper-first search, and a wallpaper-only tool won't sit in a widget slot next to your clock.

faq.question: What's the best Bible verse lock screen app for iPhone?
faq.answer: FaithWall is the best choice for lock-screen-first Scripture — it's purpose-built for wallpaper and widget verses you choose yourself. If you want lock-screen verses as a side-feature of a full Bible app instead, YouVersion's verse-of-the-day widget is the strongest built-in alternative.

faq.question: Are apps like "Bible Verse Lock Screen Widget" the same as FaithWall?
faq.answer: No. Several unrelated apps use nearly identical names — "Bible Verse Lock Screen," "Bible Verse Lock Screen Widget," "Lockscreen Bible Verse Widget" — because the search phrase itself is generic. FaithWall is a distinct, independently developed app; check the developer name and the App Store link on this page before downloading.

faq.question: Is "Faith Lock" the same app as FaithWall?
faq.answer: No, and the jobs are different. Faith Lock: Bible Prayer Focus blocks other apps on your phone until you read a Bible verse — a screen-time-management tool. FaithWall puts a Bible verse directly on your Lock Screen as a wallpaper or widget; it never blocks or gates any other app. If "faith lock" or "faith locked" is what you searched, decide first whether you want an app-blocker (Faith Lock) or passive lock-screen Scripture (FaithWall) — they solve different problems.

faq.question: Do I still need a full Bible app if I use a lock-screen verse app?
faq.answer: Yes, for reading. Lock-screen apps like FaithWall show one verse passively; they don't replace a full Bible with translations, search, or reading plans. Pair FaithWall with YouVersion, Olive Tree, or another reading app — one for seeing Scripture all day, one for sitting down to read it.
